correctness.rationale: The blue-edge local rule is exact: for blue uv the white neighbor count is d_H(u)+d_H(v). Every force deletes a white leaf-edge and requires a white isolated base vertex; cycles cannot be deleted. Conversely a leaf paired with an isolate iteratively forces every forest edge. The coefficient formula follows from the labeled-forest exponential formula, and Cayley counts every optimum. The exchange criterion is proved using leaf attachments and unique common tree U; within-class tree exchanges and star-mediated cross-class moves prove connectivity. A standalone C++17 check exhaustively compares independent forcing algorithms on all 2^(n choose 2) subsets for 3<=n<=7, checks all polynomial coefficients via independent recurrence, and confirms exchange connectivity/cross-edge counts through n=6. These finite checks corroborate, not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: The graph J(n,2)=L(K_n) is a canonical Johnson/line graph with independently studied zero forcing, matrix nullity and reconfiguration. The theorem replaces a known scalar optimum with an exact all-input characterization, a full generating function for every forcing-set cardinality, a labeled-Cayley classification of every minimizer and a connected optimum-exchange structure with exact cross-class bridge count. This is a natural infinite graph-family classification and gives exact solution-space and reconfiguration information not supplied by the scalar.
